commitResults.messageBody: Update the Java entry point, startup message, and documentation so the project consistently uses its new name.
Display a playful dragon banner, greet the user, and exit cleanly. Update the documented output and record the student's beginner experience level.

commitResults.messageTitle: Echo commands until the user says bye
commitResults.messageBody: Read user input in a loop so Toothless can echo each command, then exit with a cheerful farewell when the user enters bye.
Store user-entered tasks so Toothless can display them in numbered order when requested. Handle the list and bye commands explicitly while keeping responses friendly and varied.

Track completion state alongside each in-memory task and support the mark command so users can finish tasks while retaining Toothless's friendly tone. Show completed tasks with a star in list output, handle invalid task selections, and ignore the project-local visual diff skill so its installed files are not committed.

Allow users to reverse a task's completion state with the unmark command while preserving the friendly Toothless responses. Distinguish tasks that were already incomplete so the chatbot does not misleadingly report that their status changed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Represent tasks with a Task class
commitResults.messageBody: Encapsulate each task's description, completion state, status icon, and display formatting in a dedicated Task class. Update Toothless to store Task objects so marking and unmarking behavior lives with the data it changes and future task types can extend the shared representation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add repeatable console UI testing workflow
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce a project-specific test-ui skill and test-plan template so console behavior can be checked consistently with fail-fast transcripts. Require agents to review the plan and invoke the skill after code changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support typed tasks and clearer command guidance
commitResults.messageBody: Add Todo, Deadline, and Event subclasses with polymorphic display and plain-string scheduling details. Extend Toothless command parsing while preserving existing task actions and legacy plain-description input, and add a friendly startup guide plus an end-to-end UI regression record.
Validate malformed commands before changing task state, provide actionable Toothless-themed messages, and add interleaved UI coverage to guard against regressions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor task deletion to use collections
commitResults.messageBody: Store tasks in a private ArrayList-backed TaskList so deletion can use collection operations while preserving order. Add Toothless-themed confirmations and comprehensive UI coverage for valid and invalid deletions.
Represent the fixed command set explicitly to improve type safety and centralize keyword conversion while preserving existing chatbot behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Save tasks after list changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Task changes exist only in memory, so they disappear when Toothless
stops. Users need each supported mutation to update a durable task file.

Let's:

* save todos, deadlines, and events with their completion state
* persist the list after every command that changes it
* isolate runtime data and storage tests from personal project files

The text format keeps task fields reversible while reserving the completion
symbol for Toothless's display.

Saved tasks exist between sessions, but Toothless starts with an empty
list and cannot use them.

Let's:

* reconstruct todos, deadlines, and events from the saved file
* restore descriptions, date and time values, and completion state
* load the reconstructed list before accepting commands

Reusing the saved-field rules keeps persistence reversible and preserves the
existing completed-task display after restart.

Storage expects its directory and file to exist, and file-system failures
can stop Toothless with a raw error.

Let's:

* treat a missing data file as a clean first run
* create required directories during the first save
* replace saved data through a temporary file where possible
* report expected read and write failures without losing in-memory tasks

This keeps normal startup simple while protecting existing data from partial
writes and keeping Toothless usable when persistence is unavailable.

One malformed saved entry can stop startup and prevent valid tasks in the
same file from loading.

Let's:

* validate task type, field count, completion status, and required values
* skip malformed lines while preserving every valid task in order
* report the number of skipped entries with a friendly startup warning
* leave the original data file unchanged during recovery

This isolates corruption to the affected entries and keeps recoverable task
data available without guessing at invalid values.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add deadline date parsing and formatting
commitResults.messageBody: Centralize ISO date parsing and friendly display formatting so deadline\ndates use one consistent representation throughout the application.
Parse ISO dates before creating deadlines and retain the typed date through\nstorage. Format deadlines only when presenting them to the user.
Keep invalid command and storage dates outside the task list, and explain\nthe accepted ISO format without exposing Java exceptions to users.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UI tests for date handling
commitResults.messageBody:
Add valid and invalid deadline date cases to verify Level 8
behaviour.

Move command and task-detail validation out of Toothless and into
Parser. This separates input interpretation from application
coordination while preserving existing commands and messages.

Move console input and Toothless response formatting out of the main
application class and into Ui. This keeps Toothless focused on
coordinating parsing, task operations, and storage.

Clarify that the enum represents parsed command keywords rather than
executable command behaviour. This reserves Command for the upcoming
command abstraction without changing existing functionality.

Introduce the executable Command abstraction and move exit behaviour
into ExitCommand. This begins separating command execution from the
main application loop while preserving existing behaviour.

Move task-list display coordination into ListCommand. This further
separates command execution from the main application while keeping
task formatting within Ui.

Move task-deletion coordination into DeleteCommand. This separates task
removal from the main application while preserving validation,
persistence, and user feedback.

Move task-marking coordination into MarkCommand. This separates another
command action from the main application while preserving validation,
persistence, and user feedback.

Move task-unmarking coordination into UnmarkCommand. This keeps task
state changes outside the main application while preserving validation,
persistence, and user feedback.

Move todo creation and addition into TodoCommand. This separates todo
execution from the main application while preserving persistence and
user feedback.

Move deadline creation and addition into DeadlineCommand. Preserve date
validation, storage behaviour, and the existing user-facing format.

Move event creation and addition into EventCommand. This completes the
extraction of task-creation behaviour while preserving existing syntax,
storage, and output.

Centralize the common add, save, and confirmation workflow used by task
creation commands while keeping task-specific construction separate.

Construct concrete command objects during parsing so command
identification and argument validation remain outside the application
coordinator.

Delegate parsed actions to executable command objects so the main
application focuses on coordinating input, execution, and errors.

Delete dispatch logic made redundant by executable commands and keep
the completed command architecture focused and maintainable.
